request:
Create an accurate visitor page from these notes. Consolidate repetition and resolve old-versus-current text according to the notes.

The riverside walking route has reopened between Mill Bridge and the old ferry landing following winter repairs. The reopening covers the main gravel path only. The lower boardwalk remains closed because several supports need replacement, and the short staircase from the landing to the water is also closed. Visitors should not interpret an open gate at the bridge as permission to enter every part of the site. Temporary barriers mark the closed sections, and the route map at the entrance shows a continuous permitted walk that avoids them.

The parks team inspected the gravel path on April 12 after the contractor finished drainage work. That inspection found the path suitable for reopening under ordinary spring conditions. It was not a guarantee that the route will stay open during heavy rain. Water levels can change quickly, and the duty ranger may close the path without advance notice. A closure notice on the entrance board takes priority over an older social media post announcing the reopening. The public webpage should explain this once, clearly, rather than repeating a general warning in every paragraph.

Wheelchair users and visitors with strollers can reach the picnic area from Mill Bridge without using steps. Beyond the picnic area, a short section has loose gravel and a steep cross-slope. We do not have a completed accessibility assessment for the full route. The visitor information team should describe these known features and avoid labeling the whole walk wheelchair accessible. The nearest accessible toilet is in the bridge car park, where it is open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The toilet at the ferry landing is closed along with the lower boardwalk facilities.

Dogs are welcome on the open path if kept on a lead. The seasonal nesting zone beside the reed beds is different: dogs are excluded from that marked zone, even on a lead. The nesting restriction runs from March 1 through July 31. People may continue along the main path beside the zone, so the restriction does not close the entire walk to dog owners. Our older leaflet says that dogs are allowed throughout the park on a lead. That statement predates the nesting-zone rule and needs replacement rather than a small footnote that leaves the old claim looking current.

Cycling is permitted between Mill Bridge and the picnic area, with pedestrians having priority. Beyond the picnic area, visitors must dismount and walk their bicycles to the ferry landing. This rule applies to electric bicycles as well as conventional bicycles. Mobility aids are not classified as bicycles under this rule. Rangers have asked for the distinction to remain visible because a previous draft accidentally suggested that mobility-scooter users must leave their equipment behind. The purpose of the rule is to manage bicycle speeds on the narrower section, not to exclude people who use mobility aids.

Parking at Mill Bridge costs $3 for up to two hours or $5 for the day. Payment machines accept cards only. The park does not charge a separate walking admission fee, and visitors arriving on foot do not need to buy a parking ticket. A local volunteer group offers a free guided walk at 10 a.m. on the first Sunday of each month. Registration is required because the group is limited to twelve people. Registration reserves a guided-walk place; it does not reserve parking or waive the parking charge.

We need a visitor page that helps someone decide whether and how to visit without making them read maintenance correspondence. Give the open and closed areas first, then practical access, dog and bicycle rules, and parking information. Preserve the current rules even where older material conflicts. The guided walk is optional and should be easy to find without overshadowing the basic route information. Do not claim that the remaining repairs have a completion date: the contractor has submitted an estimate, but the parks team has not approved a work schedule.

Dogs on lead on path; excluded nesting zone March 1–July 31; older leaflet superseded.
Cycling only bridge to picnic; dismount beyond; mobility aids exempt.
$3 two hours/$5 day, cards only; no walking admission.
Guided walk first Sunday 10 a.m., free, registration cap twelve; parking separate.
